exam.title: TOEFL iBT
exam.description: Test of English as a Foreign Language - Internet-based Test for academic English proficiency

sections.name: Reading
sections.description: 2 passages, 10 questions each. Academic texts from university-level materials.

instructions.text: Read the passage and answer the questions.

stimulus.text_html:
The Formation of Coral Reefs

Coral reefs are among the most biologically diverse ecosystems on Earth, supporting approximately 25% of all marine species despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor. These remarkable structures are built by colonies of tiny animals called coral polyps...

[Full passage approximately 700 words about coral reef formation, types, and ecological importance]
According to paragraph 1, coral reefs are significant because they

options.text: are the largest structures built by living organisms
support a disproportionately large number of marine species
are found in all of the world's oceans
have existed for millions of years unchanged

stimulus.text_html: The word "remarkable" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to

options.text: unusual
impressive
ancient
fragile

stimulus.text_html: Which of the following best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence?

options.text: Coral polyps require specific conditions to survive
Symbiotic algae are essential for coral reef formation
Coral reefs can only form in tropical waters
The relationship between corals and algae is complex

stimulus.text_html: According to the passage, fringing reefs differ from barrier reefs in that fringing reefs

options.text: are larger and more diverse
form directly along coastlines
are found only in the Pacific Ocean
take longer to develop

stimulus.text_html: The author mentions atolls in paragraph 3 in order to

options.text: explain Darwin's theory of reef formation
contrast them with other reef types
describe the most common type of reef
illustrate the long-term development of reef structures

stimulus.text_html: The word "they" in paragraph 4 refers to

options.text: coral polyps
reef structures
marine species
ocean temperatures

stimulus.text_html: What can be inferred about coral bleaching from paragraph 5?

options.text: It is a natural and harmless process
It indicates stress in coral populations
It only occurs in shallow water reefs
It makes coral more resistant to disease

instructions.text: Look at the four squares [■] that indicate where the following sentence could be added to the passage.

stimulus.text_html:
Sentence to insert: This symbiotic relationship is crucial for the reef's survival.

Where would the sentence best fit?

options.text: Square A
Square B
Square C
Square D

stimulus.text_html: Which of the following statements about coral reefs is NOT supported by the passage?

options.text: They grow slowly over thousands of years
They require warm, clear water to thrive
They are immune to human-caused damage
They provide habitat for many fish species

instructions.text: Select 3 answer choices that express the most important ideas in the passage. Some choices are incorrect because they express minor ideas or are not in the passage.

stimulus.text_html: Introductory sentence: Coral reefs are complex marine ecosystems with unique formation processes.

options.text: Coral reefs support an enormous variety of marine life relative to their size
Charles Darwin was the first scientist to study coral reefs
The symbiotic relationship between corals and algae is essential for reef growth
Coral reefs are found only in the Southern Hemisphere
Different types of reefs form through distinct geological processes
Coral polyps are the largest animals in the ocean

instructions.text: Read the passage and answer the questions.

stimulus.text_html:
The Development of Writing Systems

The invention of writing is considered one of the most significant achievements in human history, marking the transition from prehistory to history. The earliest writing systems emerged independently in several regions of the world...

[Full passage approximately 700 words about cuneiform, hieroglyphics, and alphabet development]
What is the main purpose of this passage?

options.text: To compare ancient and modern writing systems
To trace the historical development of writing
To argue that one writing system is superior to others
To explain why alphabetic writing became dominant

stimulus.text_html: According to paragraph 1, the earliest writing systems were developed primarily for

options.text: religious ceremonies
recording economic transactions
preserving literary works
communicating with distant communities

stimulus.text_html: The word "emerged" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to

options.text: appeared
survived
spread
improved

stimulus.text_html: The author discusses Sumerian cuneiform in paragraph 2 in order to

options.text: show how complex early writing could be
explain why it was eventually abandoned
demonstrate its influence on later systems
provide an example of the earliest known writing

stimulus.text_html: What does the passage suggest about the relationship between Egyptian hieroglyphics and Sumerian cuneiform?

options.text: Hieroglyphics were directly copied from cuneiform
They developed completely independently
Cuneiform may have inspired the concept of writing in Egypt
Both systems used identical symbols

stimulus.text_html: According to paragraph 4, the Phoenician alphabet was significant because it

options.text: was the first writing system to include vowels
used fewer symbols than previous systems
was adopted by the Roman Empire
combined features of cuneiform and hieroglyphics

stimulus.text_html: The word "arbitrary" in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to

options.text: random
complex
meaningful
pictorial

instructions.text: Look at the four squares [■] that indicate where the following sentence could be added to the passage.

stimulus.text_html:
Sentence to insert: This innovation made literacy accessible to a much larger portion of the population.

Where would the sentence best fit?

options.text: Square A
Square B
Square C
Square D

stimulus.text_html: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage about Chinese writing?

options.text: It developed after alphabetic writing
It has remained essentially logographic
It was influenced by Phoenician script
It is no longer used in modern times

instructions.text: Select 3 answer choices that express the most important ideas in the passage.

stimulus.text_html: Introductory sentence: Writing systems have evolved significantly over human history.

options.text: The earliest writing systems used pictographic or logographic symbols
Writing was invented simultaneously in all ancient civilizations
The development of alphabets simplified writing and increased literacy
Egyptian hieroglyphics were the most beautiful writing system
Writing systems evolved from tracking commerce to recording all aspects of culture
Modern computers have made all writing systems obsolete

sections.name: Listening
sections.description: 3 lectures and 2 conversations with 28 questions total.

instructions.text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a professor during office hours.

stimulus.text_html: Topic: Discussing research paper requirements
Why does the student go to see the professor?

options.text: To ask for an extension on an assignment
To clarify the requirements for a research paper
To discuss a grade received on an exam
To request a letter of recommendation

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor suggest the student do first?

options.text: Choose a narrower topic
Read more background material
Create an outline
Schedule another meeting

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor mean when she says this: (replay audio)

options.text: The student's idea is acceptable
The student needs to think more carefully
The topic is too difficult
She is not familiar with the subject

stimulus.text_html: What requirement for the paper does the professor emphasize?

options.text: It must include primary sources
It should be at least 15 pages
It needs a strong thesis statement
It must be submitted electronically

stimulus.text_html: What will the student probably do next?

options.text: Go to the library
Start writing the paper
Email the professor an outline
Drop the course

instructions.text: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.

stimulus.text_html: Topic: Animal migration patterns
What is the lecture mainly about?

options.text: How birds navigate during migration
The evolution of migratory behavior
Threats to migrating animals
Comparing different migration routes

stimulus.text_html: According to the professor, what navigation method do birds use during the day?

options.text: Star patterns
The sun's position
Magnetic fields
Landmarks

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor imply about the magnetic sense in birds?

options.text: It is the most important navigation tool
Scientists do not fully understand it yet
It only works in certain species
It has been studied extensively

instructions.text: What two points does the professor make about young birds learning migration routes? Choose 2 answers.

stimulus.text_html: Select all that apply.

options.text: They follow experienced adults
They have an innate sense of direction
They learn routes through trial and error
They rely entirely on instinct

stimulus.text_html: Why does the professor mention Arctic terns?

options.text: To give an example of the longest migration
To explain a unique navigation method
To contrast them with other migratory birds
To describe their breeding behavior

stimulus.text_html: What can be inferred about migration research?

options.text: It has answered most questions about bird navigation
New technologies are providing new insights
It is no longer a priority for scientists
It focuses mainly on endangered species

instructions.text: Listen to part of a lecture in an art history class.

stimulus.text_html: Topic: The Impressionist movement
What aspect of Impressionism does the professor mainly discuss?

options.text: Its influence on modern art
The techniques used by Impressionist painters
The historical context of its emergence
Biographies of famous Impressionists

stimulus.text_html: According to the professor, what was revolutionary about Impressionist brushwork?

options.text: It used very small, precise strokes
It left visible brushstrokes on the canvas
It required special types of brushes
It eliminated the need for preliminary sketches

stimulus.text_html: Why does the professor mention the invention of tube paints?

options.text: To explain why Impressionists could paint outdoors
To show that new materials were expensive
To contrast professional and amateur painters
To describe changes in art education

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor suggest about the public's initial reaction to Impressionism?

options.text: It was immediately popular
It was largely negative
It varied by country
It was influenced by art critics

stimulus.text_html: Listen again to part of the lecture. What does the professor mean when she says this?

options.text: The technique was difficult to master
Critics misunderstood the painters' intentions
The paintings were considered unfinished
The colors were too bright for traditional taste

instructions.text: Match each characteristic with the correct art movement.

stimulus.text_html: Indicate whether each describes Academic painting or Impressionism.

instructions.text: Listen to a conversation between a student and a university staff member.

stimulus.text_html: Topic: Registering for housing
What is the student's problem?

options.text: She missed the housing registration deadline
She cannot afford the housing fees
Her roommate request was denied
She was assigned to the wrong dormitory

stimulus.text_html: What solution does the staff member suggest?

options.text: Applying for an exception
Joining a waiting list
Looking for off-campus housing
Contacting the housing director

stimulus.text_html: What does the staff member imply about the waiting list?

options.text: Very few students get housing from it
There is a good chance the student will get a room
It is only for upperclassmen
Students must pay a deposit to join

stimulus.text_html: Why does the student mention her scholarship?

options.text: To explain why she missed the deadline
To request a discount on housing
To ask if it covers housing costs
To prove she is a serious student

stimulus.text_html: What will the student probably do next?

options.text: Fill out the waiting list application
Contact her parents
Look for an apartment
Schedule another appointment

instructions.text: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class.

stimulus.text_html: Topic: Urban heat islands
What is the main topic of the lecture?

options.text: Global warming effects on cities
The causes and effects of urban heat islands
How to reduce air pollution in urban areas
The history of urban development

stimulus.text_html: According to the professor, what is a major cause of urban heat islands?

options.text: Increased vehicle traffic
Dark surfaces that absorb heat
Industrial pollution
Population growth

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor say about green roofs?

options.text: They are too expensive for most buildings
They can significantly reduce building temperatures
They are mainly decorative
They require constant maintenance

stimulus.text_html: Why does the professor mention asthma?

options.text: To illustrate a health effect of heat islands
To explain why trees are important
To discuss a common urban disease
To compare urban and rural health

instructions.text: What two strategies for reducing urban heat islands does the professor discuss? Choose 2 answers.

stimulus.text_html: Select all that apply.

options.text: Using reflective building materials
Banning cars from city centers
Planting more urban trees
Reducing the city population

stimulus.text_html: What does the professor imply about urban planning?

options.text: It rarely considers environmental factors
It is increasingly incorporating heat reduction strategies
It is primarily concerned with traffic flow
It has solved most urban heat problems

instructions.text: You will be asked to give your opinion on a familiar topic. You have 15 seconds to prepare and 45 seconds to speak.
Speak about the following topic. State your opinion and explain your reasons.

stimulus.text_html: Some people prefer to work in an office environment, while others prefer to work from home. Which do you prefer and why?

instructions.text: Read a passage about a campus situation, listen to two students discussing it, then speak about what you read and heard.

stimulus.text_html:
Reading Passage (45 seconds):

University to Extend Library Hours

Starting next semester, the university library will extend its operating hours from midnight to 2:00 AM during weekdays. This change is in response to student requests for more study time during exam periods...

instructions.text: The woman expresses her opinion about the library's plan. State her opinion and explain the reasons she gives for holding that opinion.

stimulus.text_html: Preparation time: 30 seconds. Response time: 60 seconds.

instructions.text: Read a passage about an academic topic, listen to a lecture excerpt, then speak about what you read and heard.

stimulus.text_html:
Reading Passage (45 seconds):

Cognitive Dissonance

Cognitive dissonance is a psychological phenomenon that occurs when a person holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values simultaneously. This creates a feeling of mental discomfort...

instructions.text: Using the example from the lecture, explain the concept of cognitive dissonance.

stimulus.text_html: Preparation time: 30 seconds. Response time: 60 seconds.

instructions.text: Listen to part of a lecture, then speak about what you heard.

stimulus.text_html: Lecture topic: Two types of animal camouflage

instructions.text: Using points and examples from the lecture, explain the two types of camouflage and how they help animals survive.

stimulus.text_html: Preparation time: 20 seconds. Response time: 60 seconds.

sections.name: Writing
sections.description: 2 tasks: Integrated (read+listen+write, 20 min) and Academic Discussion (10 min)

instructions.text: Read a passage, listen to a lecture, then write a response summarizing the points in the lecture and explaining how they relate to the reading.

stimulus.text_html:
Reading Passage (3 minutes):

The Benefits of Electric Vehicles

Electric vehicles (EVs) offer numerous advantages over traditional gasoline-powered cars. First, they produce zero direct emissions, significantly reducing air pollution in urban areas. Second, the cost of electricity for charging is substantially lower than gasoline costs. Third, EVs require less maintenance because they have fewer moving parts and don't need oil changes...

instructions.text: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on specific points made in the reading passage.

stimulus.text_html: You have 20 minutes to plan and write your response. Your response will be judged on the quality of your writing and on how well your response presents the points in the lecture and their relationship to the reading passage. Typically, an effective response will be 150 to 225 words.

criteria.name: Content
criteria.description: Accurate summary of lecture points and relationship to reading

instructions.text: Read a professor's question and two students' responses. Then write your own response contributing to the academic discussion.

stimulus.text_html:
Professor's question:

This week we've been discussing the role of technology in education. Some argue that technology enhances learning, while others believe it creates distractions. In your view, does technology in the classroom primarily help or hinder student learning? Why?

Student A (Alex): I think technology is essential in modern education. Students need to learn digital skills for the workplace, and tools like educational apps make learning more engaging...

Student B (Maria): While technology has benefits, I'm concerned about screen time and distraction. Students often use devices for social media instead of studying...

instructions.text: Write a response that contributes to the discussion. Support your ideas with reasons and examples.

stimulus.text_html: You have 10 minutes to write your response. A good response will contain at least 100 words.

criteria.name: Relevance
criteria.description: Response addresses the question and builds on the discussion

criteria.name: Development
criteria.description: Ideas are supported with reasons and examples
